docstring:
In any $2$-colouring of $\mathbb{R}^2$, for all but at most one triangle $T$ (up to
congruence), there is a monochromatic congruent copy of $T$.

The colouring is arbitrary. No measurability is assumed. `≅` compares vertices with the same
label, so the conclusion allows a relabelling `σ`.
references: [Sh76] Shader, L. E., *All right triangles are Ramsey in $E^2$!*. J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1976), 385-389.
type_pretty:
∀ (c : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → Fin 2) (T₁ T₂ : Affine.Triangle ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2))),
  ¬Erdos173.HasMonochromaticCopy c T₁ → ¬Erdos173.HasMonochromaticCopy c T₂ → ∃ σ, Congruent (T₁.points ∘ ⇑σ) T₂.points
